target.title: fix(discord): keep thread title truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Codex; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Discord thread-title prompt/context truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries for long source/channel fields.
- Uses the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper instead of raw string slicing at these caps.
- Intentionally out of scope: unrelated truncation sites, response-read bounding, config changes, and behavior outside this specific thread-title formatting boundary.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- Related to the existing OpenClaw UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** Discord thread-title prompt/context truncation should not leave a dangling surrogate when long message, channel name, or channel description text is cut at the configured limits.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0; PR head `b5bd0d0021ddb8f7bef7e29105d14e17d4efea14`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-title.generate.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-title.generate.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts
RUN  v4.1.9 /tmp/openclaw-utf16-prs/discord-thread-title
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  8 passed (8)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 20.86s
```

Regression assertion covered by this run:

```text
messageText = "m".repeat(599) + "😀tail"
channelName = "n".repeat(119) + "😀tail"
channelDescription = "d".repeat(319) + "😀tail"
completion prompt has no lone surrogate
completion prompt contains "m".repeat(599) + "..."
completion prompt contains "n".repeat(119) + "..."
completion prompt contains "d".repeat(319) + "..."
```

- **Observed result after fix:** the thread-title generation path builds completion input without malformed surrogate halves at all three changed truncation boundaries.
- **What was not tested:** full Discord deployment and live third-party completion provider delivery were not run; this proof is scoped to the touched thread-title prompt-building path.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** completion provider calls are stubbed in the focused test to capture the generated prompt without real credentials. I did not broaden the production module export surface just to expose private formatting helpers for proof.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged):** raw JavaScript string slicing can cut between a high and low surrogate at these boundaries, producing malformed text in prompt context.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-title.generate.test.ts`
- Added focused regression coverage for message, channel name, and channel description UTF-16 boundary cases.
- No known local failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Malformed truncated prompt/context text is now avoided while preserving existing caps and truncation markers.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

Discord thread-title prompt/context formatting.

How is that risk mitigated?

The patch is limited to the existing truncation boundaries, uses the existing UTF-16 helper, and is covered by focused regression coverage for all touched fields.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

ClawSweeper re-review and maintainer review.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

Waiting on CI/ClawSweeper/maintainer review. If maintainers require non-stubbed provider proof, I can add it, but I avoided expanding production exports only for proof.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

Refreshed the PR against latest main and updated the proof section with current-head validation output.
